title: HTTP Status Lookup
description: Look up common HTTP status codes and see the class, a short meaning and a typical response use. Works offline after the page loads.
intro: Enter a status code such as 404 or 429. The lookup explains the class and a practical meaning for APIs and web pages.
blurb: Look up common HTTP status codes with class and a practical meaning.
howItWorks: Enter a three-digit HTTP status code.
Press Look up. Known codes return a name, class and a short usage note.
Unknown codes still show the class from the first digit, such as 4xx client error.
examples: 404 is Not Found, a client error when the target resource does not exist.
301 is Moved Permanently, a redirect that clients and caches may store.
503 is Service Unavailable, a server error often used during maintenance.

faq.a: The list covers widely used codes from the HTTP specifications and common extensions such as 418 and 429. Obscure vendor codes may only get a class label.
No. The meanings are bundled in the page and the lookup runs locally.

faq.q: What is the difference between 401 and 403?
faq.a: 401 means authentication is missing or rejected. 403 means the server understood the request but refuses to authorize it.
